Item lookup trims the submitted slug, scans work_items then work_items_archive, and matches the exact slug; it never resolves an old opaque ID to a new name. Archived items remain eligible for this metadata access.

Visibility is USER, the stored owner or creator node, a strict ancestor of owner (or creator while unowned), an explicit participant, or the named reviewer. Stored actor objects resolve by node string here; this is the legacy rule, not a claim of born-identity fencing.

Ancestry reads parent links from the anchor toward USER with a cycle guard. Org visibility alone grants no docket access. The item owner/creator/reviewer, participants, and necessary parent links are the predicate read set.

The reservation adapter converts both missing and unreadable item lookup to false; its refusal is identical for either. Naming a resource permits only the contention projection of HELD rows, never item-read or mutation authority.

Renew/release/land require exact reservation ownership, not merely item visibility. Recover of a HELD claim instead checks stored lease/heartbeat and owner liveness, and returns only contention metadata to an unrelated caller.

A release successor must be live and able to read a nonempty associated item. These checks are necessary but not sufficient: post_mail also enforces addressing, and its refusal must roll back the entire release.

Both public names are TX_POST for every action, including the domain reads list/landing/overlap. The call runs in the resident write cycle (store.write_org under DOC_LOCK), which always ends in save_org, even for a domain read. What each outcome actually commits is measured below.

Measured on disposable SQLite with the committed document read cold (resident copy evicted): an unkeyed read commits nothing; any refusal commits nothing (domain or addressing 422, keyed conflict 409, halt/killswitch 409 before the lock); a keyed replay returns before the save and commits nothing.

A keyed read commits op_receipts and op_receipts_meta only. A keyed renew also commits reservations. A keyed release with a successor commits reservations, mail, mail_log, events, lifecycle, audiences (the first grant to a deeper report), the receiver node's mail_seq, op_receipts and op_receipts_meta, then drives one ping.

_op_file appends the receipt as the last mutation before save_org, so the receipt and its effect commit together or not at all. opreceipts.append advances meta.seq on every append; past CEILING it evicts down to TRIM_TO and moves meta.from_ms past the largest evicted mint time. opreceipts.custody/witness and _op_inflight change only in-process state.

Before the transaction the route sets a request-profiling label, a stateprobe label and an attempt-census classification. These are in-memory. The reservation names are not MANAGED_WAIT_TOOLS, so no tool-wait sidecar row and no seat_id mint occur.

The one durable diagnostic write is the slow-request trace. When handler time reaches slowtrace.THRESHOLD_MS (ORGTREE_SLOW_TRACE_MS, default 500), the access middleware calls slowtrace.emit. If <data>/diagnostics/slow-requests.jsonl is over its size cap (ORGTREE_SLOW_TRACE_MAX_KB, default 4096), emit first renames it to a single .1 sibling, replacing and so discarding any older .1. It then appends one row: route, method, status, timings, byte count and allowlisted profile fields, with no tool arguments. emit swallows its own errors, so it never fails the request. The profile-timing sink is an in-memory deque plus stdout.

facts: This specifies the current legacy reservation receipt contract. Native original-key custody/exact-result retention and runtime proof remain separate unqualified v6 work; no current receipt is represented as a complete saved response.

Both aliases and every action are transaction+post. A bare unkeyed call files no operation receipt. A keyed call must use orgtree_op_call with inner tool/args/key/epoch; envelope key fields, missing epoch, and nested receipt verbs refuse before dispatch.

Admission occurs within write_org, after caller existence/halt/killswitch checks but before reservation predicates. A retained same-key replay therefore bypasses current reservation state/item predicates. Current authentication still runs before this point; native disclosure revalidation is not claimed to exist in this legacy branch.

Fingerprint is full SHA256 of canonical tool/node/generation/normalized args. Tool aliases are distinct identities. Admission normalizes only the API text-key set first; the helper later strips/lowers action, so action spelling variants can select the same domain operation yet conflict under one key.

Admission checks key syntax, custody epoch and key age before looking for a retained row. A retained different fingerprint conflicts; a matching fence or foreign generation refuses; otherwise the row replays. Only an absent row reaches the newer-schema and eviction-watermark refusals. Receipts are found across generations and classified at their original generation and fingerprint subject.

Accepted replay returns exactly replayed/op_id/at/tool/outcome/receipt/status, not the original result and not a second helper call, save or wake. It does not repeat a post-commit effect whose prior outcome is unknown.

Immediately before save, the API appends an applied receipt in the same org transaction as reservation state and any release mail/audience changes. Refusal or a pre-commit save exception leaves none durable. The process sequence witness advances after save while the lock remains held.

The stored result is a scalar allowlist plus restricted reservation/overlap rows, capped at 128 list entries; created/updated/heartbeat timestamps, stale reasons, contention view tags and arbitrary data are omitted. Landing-query rows and stale-ID lists are not retained; count may describe more rows than the slice stores.

Post-effects list drive for this receipt class and observed is the literal unknown, even for domain-read actions. Release carrier delivery is added only after filing and saving, so it is absent from the receipt result.

Receipt schema/coverage are 1; keys permit 60-second future skew. More than 500 rows trim to 400 and raise from_ms strictly beyond the greatest evicted mint, never lower it. Retained matching rows can replay even below this watermark while epoch/age/generation checks hold; the watermark guards admission only when the row is absent.

Lookup classifies a retained row before answering. A current-epoch absent eligible reservation key is durably fenced and returns not_applied; its delayed original refuses. Under an old epoch, a matching applied row is positive evidence, but an absent row is unknown and no new fence is written. No lookup/custody classification permits executing an absent old key after uncertain restore.

Release with a successor requires the successor to be live and able to read the reservation's nonempty item; otherwise reservations.execute refuses 'successor is not a live collaborator' before any mail. An archived successor is therefore refused, so this path never reaches post_mail's deferred (non-live recipient) branch.

On a first release the api adapter calls Org.post_mail(actor, successor, body, 'status') inside the same store.write_org/DOC_LOCK cycle as the reservation transition. post_mail's addressing check (downward any depth, one hop up, sibling, or held audience) runs there, and its refusal discards the whole release, including the reservation transition.

post_mail writes into the uncommitted document: one untyped status row (from=actor, kind=status, body 'Reservation <id> was released; its release receipt is <receipt>.', relationship, message_id=id, operation_id, recv_seq with seq_origin=deposit and the mailbox identity) through deposit_mail, which also mirrors the row into mail_log and advances only the recipient node's mail_seq; one events row op=mail carrying post_mail's warnings; and one lifecycle row state=accepted, delivery=mailbox.

A reply-audience grant (grantee=successor, grantor=actor, reason '<actor> messaged directly') is appended only when the actor is a strict ancestor but not the parent of the successor, and no audience already exists. Siblings, direct reports and repeat releases add none. post_mail's warnings reach the event log, not the tool result.

mail_notify(org, actor, successor) runs before the save as a UI hint, so it fires even when the save then fails. After the save, exactly one supervisor.send_message(org, successor, ping, mail_ping=True, sender=actor, ping_reason='agent_mail') runs, and its carrier note becomes result.delivery.

The ping's delivery outcome is not observed: the receipt records post_effects expected=['drive'], observed='unknown'. A failure after the commit leaves the release, mail and grant durable, and a keyed retry replays the receipt without re-driving. A RELEASED replay returns notified:null and posts nothing.

Refusals and keyed paths have bounded contacts. 401 (token gate): no record, 0 statements. 403: 0 statements. The 409 halt/killswitch before the lock, the 422 unaddressable successor, the 422 retained-row cap, the 409 keyed conflict, the 422 stale epoch and a keyed replay all read but write nothing and wake nobody. A fresh keyed call writes its receipt (doc, log_l, meta) inside a transaction.

Hidden-contact negative control: control:hidden-contact (a statement on a pooled connection through a plain cursor) is seen as census hidden_steps >= 1, and every other reservation row shows 0. A separate ORG-STORE control, control:foreign-org-contact, is classified org-db:foreign, and no other reservation row touches a foreign org store. That control is org-store locality only; agent-level mail locality is the next fact.

Agent-level mail-locality negative control (the clause S2b ruling R1 left open). Each row's P02 `agents` block reads which agents an operation touched in two layers. Logical: the org's mail, mail_log, notices, delivering and audiences before and after the call. Physical: node ids in the statement parameters of agent-keyed rows (nodes, log_d). In all four release-notify rows (both aliases, cold and warm), every changed mail and mail_log entry, and every physically written agent row, belongs to the named successor alone (role target). The sender's own entries never change, so the contacts are never self-only, and no third agent is touched. The negative control control:third-agent-mail (a release whose notify step also posts to a third agent) is flagged both logically and physically (third_agent_mail >= 1, third_agent_rows_written >= 1). No other reservation row touches a third agent, and only release-notify produces mail.

The same holds for a successor reachable only through an audience the user granted to the sender (P02 row audience-successor:reservation.release-notify, v3 0679103, S2c finding f1): its mail and mail_log changes and its physical node row belong to that successor alone, and no third agent is touched. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

Read predicates are authenticated caller liveness/generation and runtime halt state; self identity or the target parent chain; otherwise active item membership, current role, and previous roster membership. Content is reached only after _agent_read_access returns.

facts: Legacy source contract for structural inspection and capability reporting only. The real agent HTTP door authenticates the org/node/generation, refuses archived/replaced callers and halt/killswitch, then these branches load an independent org and require the named caller live. Frozen-profile middleware additionally rejects non-loopback non-bridge clients before the diagnostic. Neither branch adds an operator identity or grants a permission.

Inspection visibility is self; team (self plus siblings sharing the same parent, not the parent or children); subtree (self plus recursive descendants); or full (rooted tree). The helper falls back to team for an empty value, but Org construction backfills a missing visibility with full before the public branch runs. These legacy defaults are distinct. Explicit hidden or unknown targets refuse as one whole request before any _safe_node call. Item membership and material-read audience grants do not broaden this structural visibility.

include_archived controls the visible universe as well as explicit target eligibility. Live-only output finally filters state exactly equal to live. The selected node row may still carry its parent id even when the parent row itself is outside visibility; that existing structural reference is not authority to inspect the parent.

Capability operations are the install-wide available_tools catalogue, not a filtered list of actions authorized for this actor/target. Restricted scope is displayed separately. Subsequent real dispatch repeats its ordinary authority checks.

Legacy deficiencies remain explicit: an unrecognized nonempty visibility falls through to full, and current generation/visibility is not fenced through completed output. The native design must not adopt these as acceptable default authority.

Caller liveness/generation and halt state; current visibility; current parent edges, child ordering and archive states define structural eligibility. Explicit targets intersect the computed visible set and retain request order and duplicates. Empty targets, including a list containing only empty strings, mean all visible rows.

A node grant/free projection also reads its current tier price and immediate non-archived children grants and prices; those children may be outside the requested output. Returned free is not a one-row read or a promise of spend authority. Archived rows return free:null.

Legacy children scans all node rows without an index argument, descendants recursively invokes it, and ordinary load_org materializes all eager nodes even for one target. Those costs are obligations for indexed native reads, never native acceptance criteria.

Neither diagnostic is present in the current legacy coverage table: coverage returns the empty unknown string, not the explicit NONE class. Their early dispatch branches nevertheless return before receipt admission/save. This classifier gap is recorded, not silently relabeled.

A syntactically accepted OP_CALL unwrap executes these reads freshly on each retry; no applied receipt is recorded, no duplicate is replayed and an unsupported-operation lookup cannot fence the key. Missing required wrapper data/nested wrappers still refuse. No fresh-operation namespace or native replay policy is inferred from that omission.

Agent authentication and halt checks use cached_org; the diagnostic branch separately calls load_org. For SQLite, _load_sqlite_org takes pooled connections and _load_lazy reads eager doc and all nodes in a short BEGIN/COMMIT snapshot before projecting. Addressing (§7.2, Org.post_mail) for an in-org agent recipient: the sender may reach any descendant, its parent (one hop up), a sibling (same parent), or anyone whose audience it holds. Everything else is refused 422 '<sender> may not address <to> — …'. Pinned: a cousin and a grandparent are refused; a reply from a deep report succeeds once the sender holds the audience its superior's mail granted. A node may address itself: the sibling clause is trivially true for sender == target (recorded, D-165).

§7.3: mail or a notice from an ancestor to a NON-child descendant that does not already hold the reverse audience grants the recipient an audience to reply to the sender directly (an 'audiences' row and the warning 'audience granted: <to> may now reply to <sender> directly'). Pinned for both tools; a second send grants nothing.
The user: only a top-level agent, or a holder of a user audience, may message 'user'; others are refused 422. orgtree_send_notice refuses the user and every outside address.

Outside parties (@org:, @mcp:, @net:, orgtree_message only): only agents; never from a sealed kiosk (read from source, not exercised); the sender must hold the ORG-INBOX (EXTERN) audience or an exact held external handle. A top-level sender without it is auto-granted it by the send (with multi-holder off, every previous holder is revoked — read from source, not exercised); anyone else is refused 422. Addressing the org's own slug or own network identity is refused. The @ext: form is retired and refuses. Pinned for @org: (top auto-grant, deep refused, self refused), @mcp: and @ext:.

Arguments pass _norm_args (a container 'to' or 'body' refuses 422 '<field> must be text, not <type>'). credits.request: only a top-level agent, or a holder of a user audience, may ask the user for credits; others are refused 422 'only top-level agents (or holders of a user audience) may ask the user for credits directly …'. A headless org refuses every request. Pinned for a deep agent.

credits.reallocate: the caller needs downward authority over the target (Org._require_authority: a strict ancestor), so reallocating oneself or one's superior is refused 422 '<actor> has no authority over <node> — authority is downward only (§7.1)'; the target must be live. A positive delta is drawn up the parent chain (_chain_acquire, cascading when cascade_alloc is on); a top-level target is bounded by the top-level grant cap. Pinned.
credits.decide: the operator decides as the user; any pending request of the org can be approved, counter-offered (any legal amount, including a reduction down to the committed floor) or denied.

credits.request: new_limit is the requested TOTAL, parsed as a number and rounded up to a whole credit ('new_limit must be a number …' otherwise); a limit at or below the current grant withdraws a pending request (or reports nothing to request) without error; a reason is required; zero headroom refuses outright; a second request AMENDS the pending one (rev + 1) rather than adding another. Request ids are 'cr' plus the count of stored requests plus one. Pinned.

credits.reallocate: delta is parsed with _arg_num ('delta must be a number (got …)' otherwise); the resulting grant is rounded UP to a whole credit, so a fractional delta can move a whole credit (+0.3 on 7 gives 8); a negative delta cannot exceed the target's unused credits ('<node> has only N unused; the rest is committed'); a zero delta is accepted as a no-op. Pinned.

credits.decide: only a pending request is decidable ('no pending credit request …' otherwise, including a second decision); action must be approve or deny; approving a request whose agent is no longer live marks it moot and changes no grant; dry=true previews a granted amount without writing and needs granted. Pinned.

Measured with the committed document read cold. credits.request: credit_requests and one event (a new or amended request, or a withdrawal); a no-op answer writes nothing. credits.reallocate: the target's grant (nodes), grant_changed notices to the target and its parent (notices, notice_log), and a 'reallocate' event; a zero delta writes only the event. credits.decide: the request row (status, granted, notice, answer_mail) and events, plus for approve/counter the grant change and its notices, plus the decision mail to the agent (mail, mail_log, lifecycle, the agent's mail_seq, and a user_outbox copy); a moot approve writes only the request row and an event. Refusals write nothing. A keyed agent call adds op_receipts and op_receipts_meta in the same save. Pinned.

orgtree_request_credits is TX_POST and orgtree_reallocate TX: a keyed call files an applied receipt in the same save and a replay returns the replay envelope with no second change. The retained result keys do not match the results: request_credits retains (id, routed, deferred), which its result never carries, so its receipt keeps NOTHING of the request (recorded legacy defect); reallocate retains (node, delta, grant) and keeps only grant. The decision route has no operation receipt. Pinned.

The two agent tools ping nobody and spark nothing; like every accepted agent call they end with hub_changed. A decision that produces a notice posts it as user mail to a live agent, then sparks mail_notify(org, @user, agent) and pings the agent once (supervisor.send_message, mail_ping, ping_reason 'credit_decision'); a moot decision sends nothing. The decision route always ends with hub_changed. Pinned with spies.

orgtree_hire and orgtree_staff come through the agent door (401/403, halt and killswitch 409, as for every agent tool). The provider gate (provider_hire_gate: the tier's provider must be enabled, installed and signed in; kiosks hold out Codex, Antigravity and OpenRouter) runs first for a hire and is a machine-state check outside the pinned set: the boundary tests patch it off and say so.

Hire destination: `target` (or its older spelling `parent`), defaulting to the caller, must be the caller or a live descendant (check_placement: '"<t>" is outside your subtree …'); only the user hires at the top level; hire_type='superior' inserts the seat above a seat in the caller's subtree (above a top-level seat only the user may). Pinned.

The new seat's scope is clamped strictly to its parent's for an agent caller: folders, every tool switch and visibility cannot exceed the parent's, and permission_mode/effort/team_charter go through set_scope, which caps permission_mode at the caller's own. Audiences use orgtree_audience's vocabulary and rules ('user' only for a top-level caller, the caller's own id, a live peer, or the caller's direct superior); a target the caller could not grant refuses the whole call. Pinned for 'user' from a non-top-level caller and for the caller's own id.

orgtree_staff inherits the seat authority unchanged (_hire_seat or _rehire_seat) and the docket authority of work_create/work_update; in rehire mode the caller needs authority over the archived node (Org.rehire: a strict ancestor, or the node's own bearer successor). An account named with `account` is validated by registry.validate_selection.

Hire: an ordinary (subordinate) hire has no defaults — add_dirs, tools (every switch) and org_visibility are required at the door and a charter by the ledger; hire_type='superior' refuses those three and permission_mode instead (it takes the anchor's). The tier must be known ('unknown tier …' lists the known ones); grant must be a non-negative whole number; seat + grant must be free on the chain from the destination up to the caller (_chain_acquire, bubbling when cascade_hire is on), else 'not enough free credits on the chain …'; max depth and max children refuse; audiences entries must be text; kickoff_kind 'notice' is refused. Every refusal is checked before the first mutation or discarded with the unsaved document. Pinned.

Staff: action is create or update ('orgtree_staff writes the docket with action …' otherwise); update needs slug; an OMITTED action is inferred (update when slug is given, else create) — the selector DSL cannot express that inference, so the registry's selector cases name the action; staff_mode is hire or rehire and must agree with `node` (a node means rehire); the docket half's own validation applies (a create needs a title). Staffing in rehire mode a node that is already LIVE is not refused: Org.rehire answers 'already live — nothing to do' and the item is still created and assigned (recorded legacy behaviour). Pinned.

Measured with the committed document read cold. A hire writes the new node (nodes) and a hire event; lifecycle.hired notices go to the parent and the new seat's peers other than the caller (notices, notice_log); a kickoff adds the kickoff mail (mail, mail_log, lifecycle); audiences write audiences and the grant's own mail; work_item writes work_items and the assignment mail. A superior insertion re-parents the anchor under the new seat, which reports to the anchor's old parent; the inserted seat's own cost is paid out of the anchor's grant (anchor 6 -> 5, inserted seat 6), budget-neutral above. Pinned.

Staff writes the seat as above, then the item in the SAME save (work_items plus the assignment mail to the seat); an update that moves an item also tells its previous owner with an @system notice; a staffing with no stored summary gets one generated boundary line (result staffing_boundary). A refusal anywhere writes nothing, EXCEPT staff in rehire mode with a `name`: the rename runs before the transaction (supervisor.rename_node takes the lock itself and moves folders), so a later refusal leaves the node renamed and still archived, and the refusal says so. A keyed call adds op_receipts and op_receipts_meta in the same save. Pinned.

orgtree_hire and orgtree_staff are TX_POST; staff in rehire mode is PRE when it carries a name (the rename moves folders before any transaction) and TX_POST without one (opreceipts.coverage). A keyed call files an applied receipt in the same save; a replay returns the replay envelope and changes nothing. Retained result keys: hire keeps node, started and account (its allowlisted name, tier and grant are not in the result); staff keeps node, started, item, created or updated, assigned_to and account. The account_binding slice (result_slice, shared with rehire and retool) is not specified here. Pinned.

A started seat is driven exactly ONCE after the save (supervisor.send_message, mail_ping, no ping_reason), whatever started it: a kickoff, a work_item or staff assignment, a rehire with waiting mail, or an audience grant that wakes the grantee. Without one of those nothing is driven and the result says the seat is IDLE. Each kickoff and each assignment sparks mail_notify(org, caller, seat), so staff with a kickoff sparks twice and posts two request mails. Every accepted call ends with one hub_changed. Recorded legacy behaviour: a hire started only by an audience grant is told 'its first turn starts on your kickoff' although no kickoff was sent. Pinned with spies.

Source read set: the caller, the destination and its chain up to the caller (free amounts, grants, scopes, depth and child counts), tier prices and the tier ceiling, the org's defaults (visibility, tools, account, cascade_hire), the audience table, and for staff the work items; the harness choice for an OpenRouter tier is a provider read made before DOC_LOCK (new_hire_harness).

facts: orgtree_op_lookup is a receipt VERB on POST /api/agent, not a tool card: it needs the caller's agent token (401 otherwise) and, like every agent tool, is refused 409 while the caller is halted or the org killswitch is latched (supervisor.halt.blocked runs first, pinned for a halted caller); it is then answered by _op_lookup_call BEFORE the restart/relaunch gates and the write cycle, because a lookup performs none of those operations. A caller can only ask about its OWN keys: the row is found by (caller node, key), so asking about another agent's key finds nothing and fences that key in the caller's own namespace (pinned).

op_key is required ('a lookup needs the `op_key` it is asking about') and for_tool is required ('a lookup needs `for_tool` …'); for_args is normalised exactly as admission normalises it, so the two fingerprints of one call agree. The row under the key is classified before any claim: a different fingerprint is `conflict`; a matching applied row is `applied` (also under a rotated epoch — durable positive evidence); a fence is reported as the fence; a call with the key executing in this process is `running`; a verb that never reaches the transaction is `unknown`/unsupported_operation; under a rotated epoch an absent row is `unknown`/epoch_rotated and nothing is fenced. Otherwise the key is FENCED and the answer is `not_applied` when the verb's coverage class makes absence provable, `unknown`/pre_transaction_step when the verb also works outside the transaction. Pinned.

The agent-side client (mcptool.call_api) asks only after the answer to a keyed call was LOST, under the original key and epoch, and never reissues the call itself. A lookup REFUSED as an unknown verb ("orgtree_op_lookup" in the refusal) means the backend predates receipts: the client answers state unknown, reason unsupported_build (fb501a21). Pinned with the transport patched.

Only a lookup that finds nothing (current epoch, receipted verb, not running) writes: one op_receipts row with outcome 'fenced' (op_receipts, op_receipts_meta) under DOC_LOCK in its own save, then witnessed. Every other answer writes nothing. The fence is what makes `not_applied` true: a delayed original under that key is refused at admission ('op_key refused (fenced) …', 422) and changes nothing. Pinned.

A lookup is never itself keyed (a question must not become an operation with its own key); its durable trace is the fence row. A repeated lookup of a fenced key answers from the fence (with its `at`) and writes nothing. Pinned.
A lookup drives nobody, sparks nothing and does not broadcast: it returns from agent_call before the dispatch tail that ends in hub_changed, including when it fences. Pinned with spies.
